questions.prompt: What is the extra day in a leap year?
questions.explanation: A leap year adds 29 February, taking the year from 365 days to 366.

questions.prompt: Why does the calendar sometimes need an extra day?
options: A year of seasons is a little longer than 365 days
questions.explanation: The small amount of time beyond 365 days adds up. Leap days help keep calendar dates in step with the seasons.

questions.prompt: Why will 2100 not be a leap year?
options: All years ending in 00 lose the day
It ends in 00 but does not divide exactly by 400
questions.explanation: Years ending in 00 have an extra check. 2100 is five groups of 400 plus 100 left over, so it skips the leap day.

title: Is 2100 a leap year? Why the calendar skips it

sources.name: NASA Space Place — What Is a Leap Year?

practice: Try General Knowledge for more questions about dates, discoveries and the world around us.

sections.html:
No. In the Gregorian calendar, 2100 is not a leap year because it is divisible by 100 but not by 400. February will have 28 days, and the year will have 365.

The catch is easy to miss: “every four years” has an exception. NASA’s calendar guide gives the full rule.
sections.title: Is 2100 a leap year?

sections.html:
“Divisible” means a division leaves no remainder. For example, 12 divides evenly by 4; 13 does not.

  1. Not divisible by 4? It is an ordinary year.
  2. Divisible by 4, but not by 100? It is a leap year.
  3. Divisible by 100? It is a leap year only if it also divides evenly by 400.

2100 passes the first check: 2100 ÷ 4 = 525. But 2100 ÷ 400 = 5.25, so it fails the final one.
sections.title: The leap-year rule, one check at a time

sections.html:
2000 ÷ 400 = 5, with nothing left over. That century year kept its extra day. Compare:

  • 1900: no leap day.
  • 2000: a leap year.
  • 2100: no leap day.
  • 2400: a leap year.
sections.title: Why was 2000 a leap year, then?

sections.html:
A cycle of seasons lasts a little less than 365¼ days. Adding a full day every four years would slowly add too much time. Skipping three century leap days in each 400-year cycle makes the calendar a closer match.

NASA Space Place explains why the small difference adds up. It is a calendar correction, not Earth deciding to take a day off.
sections.title: Why leave out an extra day?

sections.html: These are Gregorian rules. Countries adopted them at different times, so old dates need care. See why Britain skipped eleven calendar dates in 1752.
